definitions.explanation: Making something larger in amount or volume. Commonly used for food products, medicine dosages, and material quantities.

examples.japanese: ⟦{期間|きかん}{限定|げんてい}→期間限定：09744_kikangentei⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧20%{増量|ぞうりょう}。
⟦{薬|くすり}→薬：00793_kusuri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{量|りょう}→量：03799_ryou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{増量|ぞうりょう}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I had my medication dosage increased.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦スナック→スナック：27527_sunakku⟧{菓子|がし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{今月|こんげつ}→今月：00720_kongetsu⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦{中身|なかみ}→中身：01483_nakami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{増量|ぞうりょう}⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: This snack has extra contents only this month.

notes: Composed of {増|ぞう} (increase) + ⟦{量|りょう}→量：03799_ryou⟧ (quantity). Very commonly seen on food packaging in Japan as a marketing term: {増量|ぞうりょう}⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧ (now with more!), 20%{増量|ぞうりょう} (20% extra). The opposite is ⟦{減量|げんりょう}→減量：13355_genryou⟧ (reduction in quantity; also weight loss in sports/dieting). Common collocations: {増量|ぞうりょう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to increase the amount), {増量|ぞうりょう}⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧ (currently offering extra), {増量|ぞうりょう}⟦{分|ぶん}→分：26216_bun⟧ (the extra portion).
